entry.title: Access status rechecked 19 Oct 2026, 05:22 UTC: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price, rate-limit wording and model aliases unchanged (jev-latest still on jev-1.13.0; TypeSafe has published no date for the move to 1.14). Home keeps its four notices; none retired.

When Jev fails: ohmyjev (a Claude Code module with Bash, Write/Edit and exfiltration gates) joins the checklist after its pi and omp adapters were read in full, so it counts 80 implementations with every failure cell recorded. On a Jev error 40 stop or hold the action, 22 fall back, 10 let it through, 5 return no decision and 3 are advisory; the action goes ahead in 19 of 80.

Claude Code and MCP: ohmyjev's bypass cell is recorded and it is counted on the failure checklist; the short answer over ten guardrails is unchanged. jkudish/jev-mcp rows now cite the commit their cells were read at (53fe575, 0.11.0), with the 0.13.0 and 0.14.1 checks listed separately (also on products).

Alternatives: Liquid AI d1-ultra, Mouse-1 (preview) and Eevo (Upright) added as hosted decision APIs from other providers, with status, published prices and data terms quoted from their own pages; 37 substitutes, 7 of them hosted APIs. Their claims against Jev are the vendors' own; no graded comparison.
Content moderation (11 cells) and support-ticket triage (9 cells): failure cells now lead with the failure checklist's terms, with the detail on the line below. No outcome changed.

Products: beside the VentureBeat-relayed Vercel adoption claim, Vercel's own AI Gateway production-index figures (35.3% of paid AI Gateway teams in Jev's first two weeks; 0.27% of gateway spend over that period). Reported; Vercel sells gateway access to Jev.
New dated report: the failure map completed with ohmyjev, the jev-mcp commits, and what Liquid AI d1-ultra, Mouse-1 and Eevo publish about prices and data terms.

Access status rechecked 18 Oct 2026, 05:17 UTC: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price, rate-limit wording and model aliases unchanged (jev-latest still on jev-1.13.0; TypeSafe has published no date for the move to 1.14). Home keeps its four notices; none retired.

When Jev fails: two Claude Code guards join the checklist (claude-model-guard fails open on a Jev error; claude-jev-advisor's Windows delete guard holds), so it counts 79 implementations with every failure cell recorded. On a Jev error 40 stop or hold the action, 22 fall back, 9 let it through, 5 return no decision and 3 are advisory; the action goes ahead in 18 of 79. A line explains why second-look is counted here but not on the browser page.

Claude Code and MCP guardrails: three guardrails read at pinned commits are added (claude-model-guard, claude-jev-advisor, ohmyjev). New short answer: of ten guardrails read in source, two hold or stop when Jev fails, one falls back, two are shadow or log-only, one is advisory, three fail open and one returns a verdict only. ohmyjev is not yet in the failure-checklist count.

Coding agents: cells now use the failure checklist's terms. Correction: on a Jev error the 13 integrations that act on Jev's answer are 3 fail-closed, 9 fallback and 1 fail-open (the earlier split "5 let the call run, 3 hold, 5 fall back" did not match the cells). Bypass cells say "recorded". No outcome changed.

Trading and fraud gates, and browser and computer use: cells use the failure checklist's terms and colours; bypass cells say "recorded", with what happens without Jev in the detail. On a Jev error the 4 trading bots are 2 fail-closed and 2 fallback; both fallbacks can still place a new order. No outcome changed.

Products: the ledger has 113 rows (14 added: three Claude Code guards, three game and robot demos, eight projects). For 100 the Jev call was read at a pinned commit; none of the 113 is independently verified in production. Of 7 published production or cost claims, 5 are online with the same text and 2 relayed by VentureBeat were not rechecked.

Model IDs and aliases: on 18 Oct jev-latest still points to jev-1.13.0. Opper now lists typesafe/jev-1.14.0 (alias typesafe/jev-preview; its jev-latest alias stays on 1.13.0), so 5 of 6 routes list a 1.14 ID. Vercel lists a 32,000-token context window for all three Jev IDs; it equals TypeSafe's per-question limit, but Vercel does not define the field.

TypeScript: @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.7.0 keeps the 0.6.0 failure path (timeout, retries, missing-key error and default model). Validation errors now reject the returned promise, request bodies of 1 KiB or more are zstd-compressed by default on Node 22.15+, and the package needs Node 22.

Alternatives: Liquid AI d1-ultra and Mouse-1, hosted decision models launched in the last days, are noted with their launch-page prices; their performance claims are the vendors' own, and their terms were not read. They are not yet evaluated or listed as rows.

Research report of 18 October 2026: failure terms aligned across pages, three Claude Code guardrails read, and the products ledger rechecked. It covers what was read, what changed and what is still not verified.

Access status rechecked 16 Oct 2026, 05:21 UTC: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price unchanged. TypeSafe released Jev 1.14 under jev-preview (jev-latest still on jev-1.13.0, moving in about a week per TypeSafe); its models page no longer lists rate-limit numbers (set per organization, shown in the console); image input, a Box question type and 262k long context are opt-in experiments. Home shows four notices; the hidden Series A notice retired at the end of its seven-day shelf life.

When Jev fails: the last 11 bypass cells (judge tools 4, frameworks 3, browser agents 3, email 1) and the last malformed cell were read at their pinned commits. Every failure cell (no key, error, malformed answer, below threshold, bypass) is now recorded for all 77 implementations. Bypass recorded for 77 of 77; 13 are "none found". Malformed answer: 35 fail closed, 24 fall back, 11 fail open, 4 no decision, 3 advisory. Seven existing cell texts were corrected without changing their terms.

Model IDs and aliases: TypeSafe released Jev 1.14 (jev-1.14.0) under jev-preview on 14 Oct; jev-latest still points to jev-1.13.0, and TypeSafe says it moves in about a week. OpenRouter, Vercel and Netlify list 1.14; Cloudflare, Opper, Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry did not list it on 16 Oct. Image input, a Box question type and 262k long context are opt-in experiments that TypeSafe calls not production-ready. The page is retitled "Jev 1.14 preview, 1.13 and jev-latest (TypeSafe AI): model IDs and aliases by route"; its URL is unchanged.
